record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: For a system where directed-acyclic-graph jobs arrive over time, each job consists of tasks with precedence constraints, and the scheduler must choose both which jobs to run and which tasks within each job to run on n servers, what is the optimal allocation policy for minimizing mean job response time?

evidence.quote: Even with these simplifications, finding the optimal allocation policy is a very hard open problem

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a queueing system with $n$ identical servers. Jobs arrive over time according to a stochastic arrival process (for concreteness, take a Poisson process of rate $\lambda$). Each arriving job is a directed acyclic graph (DAG) whose vertices are tasks and whose directed edges encode precedence constraints: a task may begin processing only after all of its predecessor tasks have completed. Each task has a (random) service requirement drawn from a known distribution, and at most one task may be processed on a server at a time; a server processes at most one task at a time, and tasks are non-preemptive (or, equivalently, preemptive — both variants are of interest). The DAG structure and task sizes of each job are revealed upon arrival.

A scheduling policy must, at every moment, decide (a) which of the currently present jobs to work on and (b) which eligible tasks (those whose predecessors have completed) of each chosen job to assign to which of the $n$ servers. Let $T$ denote the response time of a job (the time from its arrival until the completion of its final task), and let $\mathbb{E}[T]$ denote the long-run mean response time over all jobs.

Problem. Determine the scheduling policy that minimizes $\mathbb{E}[T]$, and characterize the resulting optimal value as a function of $n$, the arrival rate, and the joint distribution of DAG structure and task sizes.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of optimally scheduling DAG-structured jobs across multiple servers to minimize mean response time is widely regarded as an open problem in queueing theory; even simplified versions (fixed DAG, identical task sizes) remain unresolved. No general optimal policy is known; recent work focuses on heuristics and approximation guarantees.

status_evidence.claim: The optimal allocation policy for DAG-job scheduling to minimize mean response time is stated as an open problem.
